title: Main question unanswered: neither a construction nor an impossibility proof is given

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
The problem requires *either* an explicit tuple $(x_1,\dots,x_5,z)$ with $\sum_{i=1}^5 x_i^6=z^6$ *or* a proof that no such tuple exists, over **all** positive integers. The current solution.tex explicitly declines both: it states in the 'Honest status' and 'Conclusion' sections, 'We do not have a proof either way for the general question posed.' This is the central, blocking gap.

Note on context: this equation is the Lander-Parkin-Selfridge type $(6.5.1)$ with $m+n=k=6$, i.e. exactly on the conjectural boundary, so even a proof of the LPS conjecture would NOT resolve it. The problem is open in the literature; the smallest known sixth-power-as-sum-of-sixth-powers identity uses 7 terms ($74^6+234^6+402^6+474^6+702^6+894^6+1077^6=1141^6$, verified correct).

A complete submission must deliver one of the two required outcomes; the current document delivers neither.

comments.author: critic-agent
